subject: PrivDeploy: license carveouts & staged-audit request
messages:
From: Ankit Shah <ankit.shah@procure.starlighthealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlighthealth.com>, legal@starlighthealth.com
Date: 2027-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify license boundary + evidence for private deploy (MSA/Exhibit B)

Irene —

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. Before our internal legal/infosec review tomorrow they flagged two items they want explicit language for in the MSA/Exhibit B for the private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment:

1) License boundary: confirmation we are licensed to run the model for our customers and for derivative outputs, but Starlight needs a short clause that restricts Redwood from making backups of our dataset or using our customer data to fine‑tune external models.

2) Audit/evidence: our compliance team needs an auditable procedure — ideally a staged window where Starlight can witness a snapshot/export of runtime binaries, operator logs, and a short proof of access to demonstrate we can access the environment for incident response. They mentioned something like an "escrow-lite" approach (sealed snapshot + time‑boxed witness).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide this evidence and share a suggested passage we can circulate internally? If you have a redline we can review that would be great.

Attachments: none from our side yet.

—Ankit
Procurement, Starlight Health

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-09T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify license boundary + evidence for private deploy (MSA/Exhibit B)

Team —

Forwarding Starlight's asks (below). They want two narrow things: 1) limited license language (no backup/fine‑tune use of customer data) and 2) a reproducible, auditable evidence pathway — they used the term "escrow-lite."

Quick asks:
- Lauren: can you draft a short clause that protects Redwood IP while giving Starlight explicit assurances on data use and backup restrictions? Keep it symmetrical but shopable.
- Ben/Karthik: confirm whether we need to recommend Dedicated vs VPC for their use case (commercial impact) and whether the proposed evidence path affects pricing (e.g., on‑site witnesses or time‑boxed console access).

I'll draft a consolidated redline to send back to them but want legal signoff first.

Thanks —
Irene
Senior Program Manager, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal legal team)
Date: 2027-12-10T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify license boundary + evidence for private deploy (MSA/Exhibit B)

Irene —

Draft guidance below. I kept the language practical and limited to operational assurances (no open‑ended IP transfers). Two pieces: 1) license/data use carveout, 2) staged witness protocol (non‑exclusive, time‑boxed). If acceptable I'll prepare a redline (RDW_MSA_redlines_v3.docx).

(1) License boundary (proposed language snippet):
"Customer Data and Derivatives. Customer retains all ownership in Customer Data. Redwood is licensed to execute models to provide the Services and to produce Outputs on behalf of Customer. Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train, fine‑tune, or improve any external models, nor will Redwood retain copies of Customer Data for the purpose of model development, except to the limited extent necessary for short‑term operational troubleshooting. Any retention beyond 30 days requires Customer consent in writing."

(2) Staged witness / escrow‑lite (proposed procedure summary):
- Redwood will provide a time‑boxed witness window (max 4 hours) during which Customer may observe 
  (a) a sealed snapshot hash of the deployed runtime and configuration artifacts,
  (b) operator audit logs for the requested interval, and
  (c) ephemeral, read‑only console access for a named Customer witness.
- Redwood will produce a signed attestation (Operator Access Attestation) listing what was made available.
- No export of Redwood proprietary binaries or source will be provided; the snapshot is a hash and metadata plus operator logs. If a Customer requires full binary handover, parties will negotiate a separate Exhibit C (license for source/binaries).

Risk notes: the witness window increases operational coordination; for higher frequency or extended windows we should consider a commercial uplift. Also need to confirm whether law enforcement/subpoena handling language is acceptable to them.

If you want, I'll add alternate wording that allows a short (signed) escrow deposit with a third‑party custodian for snapshots — that is heavier but sometimes makes infosec teams comfortable.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-10T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify license boundary + evidence for private deploy (MSA/Exhibit B)

Quick commercial note:
- For Starlight's scale (they've told us ~5M monthly tokens, multi‑region), recommending Dedicated pool will reduce audit friction but will change price and commitment. VPC deployment + witness window is doable with standard dedicated SLA adders.
- If they want repeated witness windows or on‑site presence we should add a line item (audit coordination fee + staff day rate).

I'll draft two short bullets for the order form: 1) recommended deployment (Dedicated Capacity) and 2) optional Audit Coordination Addendum (day‑rate pricing). Once legal confirms language, I can include pricing in the redline package.

—Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlighthealth.com>, Ankit Shah <ankit.shah@procure.starlighthealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify license boundary + evidence for private deploy (MSA/Exhibit B)

Maria / Ankit —

Thanks for the clear ask. Please find attached our initial redline (RDW_MSA_redlines_v3.docx) and a proposed Operator Access Attestation (privdeploy-Exhibit-Operator-Attestation.pdf). Highlights:

- License snippet limits retention beyond 30 days without consent and prohibits use of Customer Data for training external models (we can tighten retention window if you prefer).
- Staged witness mechanics: time‑boxed 4‑hour witness window, sealed snapshot hash + operator logs, and ephemeral read‑only console for one named witness.
- Commercial: Ben recommends Dedicated for audit efficiency; optional Audit Coordination Addendum covers staffing and on‑site requests (pricing to be included in the order form).

Attachments included: RDW_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (redline), privdeploy-Exhibit-Operator-Attestation.pdf (attestation template), starlight_audit_schedule.xlsx (sample witness windows).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the 4‑hour witness window and the "no full binary handover" position are acceptable.
2) If Starlight wants a sealed third‑party escrow of the runtime artifacts, note that will require separate Exhibit C and affect timeline/costs.
3) If acceptable, we'll circulate a single consolidated MSA/Order Form redline and route via DocuSign (link included).

We aim to have a final redline for your procurement/legal by EOD Thursday 12/16 to keep the Q1 onboarding timeline.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Program Manager, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx), privdeploy-Exhibit-Operator-Attestation.pdf (pdf), starlight_audit_schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlighthealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@starlighthealth.com, ankit.shah@procure.starlighthealth.com
Date: 2027-12-13T16:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: license carveouts & staged-audit request

Irene / team —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the redline. High level: the license language looks acceptable to our legal counsel subject to one edit (shorten the operational retention window from 30 days to 14 days).

Regarding the witness protocol we are comfortable with a 4‑hour time‑boxed window and the hash + logs approach. A couple of clarifications we need before signoff:
- Can the read‑only console session be recorded (screen capture) by Starlight during the window? That would help our audit trail.
- If we name a single witness, can we swap that person for a backup (e.g., different custodian) within the same window?

We do not need binary handover at this time. As for deployment mode, procurement prefers VPC first; if audit ops are problematic we may convert to Dedicated after pilot. So please keep both options in the order form.

I'll circulate the small edits (14‑day retention note + console recording clause) and expect to return a consolidated redline by EOD Friday 12/17.

Thanks —
Maria Gomez
Senior Manager, Vendor Procurement
Starlight Health
